plan.title: After a miss, today's step is the same or easier, never a jump

context.text: Morgan! You've got this tonight. 2 min jog, 1 min walk around the block at 6:30.
work blew up, not happening today sorry

transcript.text: Morning, Morgan! Friday got swallowed by work, so today we get it back. 6:30 pm around your block: 1.5 min jog, 1.5 min walk, 3 rounds, the same ones you handled Wednesday. That's only about 15 minutes, and it keeps the mile by Nov 14 in reach. Send me the Strava screenshot after. You in?
Let's go, Morgan. 6:30 pm, around the block, and I'll be waiting on that Strava screenshot. 💪

checks.reason: Names today's step: 1.5 min jog, 1.5 min walk, 3 rounds, around the block at 6:30 pm.
"Friday got swallowed by work" names the miss lightly with no guilt or urgency.
Runs about seven sentences with extra detail ("That's only about 15 minutes", "keeps the mile by Nov 14 in reach"), well over one to three sentences.
Ends with one question, "You in?", and does not ask about time.
Gives what, where (around your block), when (6:30 pm) and how long (about 15 minutes).
Plain text with no markdown or hashtags.
Warm, direct and pushy-level without overfamiliarity.
Two sentences with no question, which fits the limit.
Encouraging and free of guilt or pressure.
Plain words with a single emoji as punctuation.
Warm and sincere, with a single emoji and no overfamiliarity.

conversation.reason: The kickoff is correct: it eases to 1.5/1.5, names the miss lightly and asks only if they're in. But the reply restates "6:30 pm, around the block", which the regression case says should not happen after a short yes.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the regression well: the kickoff names the missed Friday lightly, eases the step below Friday's, and asks one thing, with no time re-asked. It falls short on length in the kickoff and restates the time and place in the reply to a short yes.
